$comment: How AFC-B meets owner rules R55 to R61 (2026-09-17). Read by ~/.claude/skills/security-rules/scripts/check-security.mjs. Stack: Django + DRF on MySQL, one database role, access decided in views. Rule text: ~/.claude/OWNER-RULES.md section D; the mapping table is in WEBSITE/CLAUDE.md.

rls.na: MySQL through one Django role: the database has no row-level security to declare. Every row a handler touches is scoped in the view (validate_token for the session, org_can_event / _is_event_admin / role gates for who may act, canonical_profile for the user's own row). The runtime proof of that scoping is security/idor-cases.json.

the public transfer feed (/teams transfers tab): public by design, team_id only narrows a public list; writes to TeamTransfer happen elsewhere behind the team gates
payload is the OAuth state the server signed and consumed once (state.consume); the user_id in it was written by us before the provider round trip, never sent by the client
the one **create is duplicate_event copying the model's OWN columns (duplicate_field_values(source), the contract's inverted duplication); the request body only names the source event
fields is a dict this code builds by hand (user_id, phone, direction, body...) from a signature-verified Meta webhook; no request key reaches the ORM unnamed
token here is a signed back-channel logout JWT (RFC 8417 security event) posted to the partner; it is not a cookie and never reaches a browser
a helper, not a handler: device_from_request reads one token off the sign-in body for the callers (login, two-factor verify), which authenticate first; its write (remember) runs after a passed factor
public read-only endpoints (the rankings ladders, allowed under R58); the only .update( in the file is a dict; month and season are parsed with try/except and a code
the file is decoded as text in memory and parsed line by line, never stored; capped at MAX_LOG_BYTES (25 MB) since 2026-09-18; no content type is trustworthy for a game client's .log
the system f-string interpolates a staff-maintained knowledge file (load_knowledge) and a constant invite link; the admin's text goes in the user message

the cap is per ORGANIZATION: Organization.ocr_free_reads_left, decremented and refunded in afc_ocr/services/extract.py (SharedCredentials); past it the organizer's own key pays (key_required_response)

A recorded decision, not an oversight (WEBSITE/CLAUDE.md, R63 row, 2026-09-18) and carried in the security debt ledger as MEDIUM; revisit with a Fernet field if payouts ever stop needing the raw value
GoogleAuthError.message: our own class, our own sentence about the Google sign-in step that failed (afc_auth/connections/google.py). No library text reaches the user.
GoogleAuthError.message, as above. The sign-in path's own wording, written for the person signing in.
a ValueError our own restore service raises with a written sentence ('that account was not deleted'), answered with the code not_deleted.
services.DrawError.message: the draw engine's own refusals ('this group is full', 'that team is already seeded'), which are the answer the organizer needs.

_ParticipantResolutionError.message and ProviderError.message: our own classes. The first names the row of the uploaded result that could not be matched to a team, the second says which OCR provider refused and why; both are written by us.

ProviderError / RuntimeError / FileNotFoundError raised by afc_ocr's own services with written messages (a model that is not enabled, an image that is not readable). The OCR screen shows them so the organizer can fix the upload.

the remaining sites are the market's own validation sentences; the one bare-Exception leak in this file was fixed on 2026-09-22 and answers through afc_auth.api_errors.internal_error.
PollFieldError.message: names the poll field that is wrong, which is the whole point of the message.
ParseProblem.message: names the line and column of the uploaded file that could not be read. An importer that says 'something went wrong' is unusable.

GroupCapacityError, WriteRefused, ProviderError and ValueErrors raised by this module's own parsers (_clean_required_connections and friends), each with a written sentence. The two sites the checker used to report inside commented-out code are no longer counted (codeLines, 2026-09-22).

They are deliberately NOT restricted to images (a person locked out sends a screenshot, a PDF receipt or a log), so the image gate is the wrong tool; they are never served back as executable content.

the Meta webhook: the signature is verified over the RAW body with a constant-time compare BEFORE the body is parsed (R72), the handshake parameters are checked and refused with a sentence, and the payload is read field by field with defaults.

the OAuth endpoints: client id, redirect URI, scope and state are each validated against the registered application before anything is issued.

https.enforcedBy: nginx on the VPS (deploy/vps/nginx-afc.conf): port 80 answers 301 to https for both hosts; HSTS max-age=31536000 includeSubDomains on both 443 server blocks

uploads.note: afc_auth/image_utils.py require_image_upload is the one image door: it decodes the bytes with Pillow, allows JPEG / PNG / WEBP / GIF / HEIF only, caps at 10 MB and returns a code for the refusal. A file that calls it is typed, sniffed and capped; the rule judges every other file exactly as before. _clean_logo_upload (afc_sso/provisioning.py) is the second door, used by the partner and sponsor logo paths: size first, then a Pillow decode that must agree the bytes are PNG / JPEG / WEBP, then a dimension cap, then a rename so no attacker-chosen extension reaches the media directory.

validation.note: AFC has no schema layer and is not getting one retro-fitted: every handler reads its own fields with request.data.get, coerces the type it needs and refuses with a coded 400 (owner rule R35). That is the house idiom, it is what the 800-odd endpoints already do, and swapping it for serializers everywhere would be a rewrite with no behaviour change. The files listed below were READ on 2026-09-22 rather than waved through.
